scope.description: Four single-voter prefixes with no snapshot, each restarted with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled in a goroutine and observed for up to 8000ms. The pairs are (MaxAppendEntries 16, staged commit index 2049 and 2050) and (MaxAppendEntries 64, staged 8193 and 8194); each event reports the entries in the replayed range, the entries that become commit tuples and the batches those tuples need.
assumptions: The prefix applies commands one at a time until the store's commit index reaches the target and reports the value it reached.

The delivered-tuple count comes from scanning the replayed range for LogCommand, LogBarrier and LogConfiguration entries, which is what prepareLog accepts at the default protocol version 3; the replayed range contains one no-op, so the tuple count is one below the staged index.
No snapshot exists on any prefix, so the replay starts at index 1 and the whole range is delivered.
The block is judged by non-return within 8000ms plus a stack sample naming the replay frames; permanence comes from the source, since the channel's only consumer starts after the replay returns.
excluded: No production store and no multi-node group; the measurement concerns the channel boundary, not the reachability of such a range in a deployment.
Only two batch sizes are placed, so intermediate sizes are bracketed by the arithmetic rather than measured.

basis.prefix: For each case the harness creates an in-memory transport and a commit-tracking log store, configures inmemConfig with RestoreCommittedLogs true, the case's MaxAppendEntries, SnapshotThreshold 1<<30 and SnapshotInterval one hour, calls BootstrapCluster with the single voter and NewRaft with a fresh MockFSM, waits for real leadership and applies one command at a time until the store's commit index reaches the target. It records the commands applied, the log's last index, the staged commit index, the tuples in the replayed range, the batches those tuples need and the entry-based count, then shuts the prefix down. The restart creates a new transport on the same address, copies the config with RestoreCommittedLogs true and calls NewRaft in a separate goroutine on the same stores with a fresh MockFSM; the main goroutine waits up to 8000ms and, on non-return, samples all goroutine stacks and reports the excerpt around the first frame naming restoreFromCommittedLogs.
basis.responsibility: NewRaft owns completion of its own startup work; the size of the replay it performs is set by the entries that become commit tuples, so the same channel boundary must appear at the same number of delivered batches whatever the batch size.

comparisons.description: A replay of exactly 128 delivered batches at the 16-batch size fills the FSM channel without exceeding it, so NewRaft must return.
A replay of 129 delivered batches at the 16-batch size needs one more batch than the channel holds, so NewRaft must still return.
A replay of exactly 128 delivered batches at the default 64-batch size fills the FSM channel without exceeding it, so NewRaft must return.
A replay of 129 delivered batches at the default 64-batch size needs one more batch than the channel holds, so NewRaft must still return.

before.description: Two single-voter prefixes at Config.MaxAppendEntries 16 with no snapshot, built so that their persisted commit index ends at 2049 and 2050. Each prefix is restarted with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, NewRaft is called in a goroutine, and the harness waits up to 8000ms. Both events report the entries in the replayed range and, separately, the number of entries in that range that become commit tuples and the batches those tuples need.
assumptions: The prefix applies commands one at a time and stops as soon as the store's commit index reaches the target, and the harness reports the value it actually reached.
The tuple count is derived by scanning the replayed range for LogCommand, LogBarrier and LogConfiguration entries, which is what prepareLog accepts at the default protocol version 3.
No snapshot exists on either prefix, so the replay starts at index 1 and the whole range is delivered.
The block is judged by non-return within 8000ms plus a stack sample naming the replay frames; permanence comes from the source, since the channel's only consumer starts after the replay returns.
excluded: No production store, no multi-node group and no default SnapshotThreshold: the point of this case is the boundary in batches, not the reachability of the range under default settings.
Only two points are placed, one batch below and one batch above the capacity, so no finer scan of the edge is attempted.

responsibility.before: NewRaft owns completion of its own startup work; the size of the replay it performs is set by the entries that become commit tuples, so the caller cannot infer the reachable replay from the log's index range alone.
responsibility.after: NewRaft owns completion of its own startup work; the size of the replay it performs is set by the entries that become commit tuples, so the same channel boundary must appear at the same number of delivered batches whatever the batch size.

before.description: A replay of exactly 128 delivered batches fills the channel without exceeding it, so NewRaft must return.

A replay of 129 delivered batches needs one more batch than the channel holds, so NewRaft must still return; the pair with the 128-batch case places the bound at the channel's capacity in delivered batches rather than at a count of replayed log entries.

revision_reason: Extends the boundary harness to a second batch size: alongside the 16-batch pair it now places the replay on both sides of the capacity at the library default of 64 batches, using stages 8193 and 8194 which deliver 8192 and 8193 tuples, that is 128 and 129 batches. The earlier pair is unchanged apart from its case names carrying the batch size; the purpose is to show the boundary is 128 delivered batches at more than one MaxAppendEntries value rather than a property of one setting.
